extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, grant applicants, research administrators, and institutional officials
extracted.subtask_description: A roundup of NIH extramural news items and policy updates relevant to preparing and submitting grant applications, managing awards, and understanding review outcomes. Includes brief guidance on new formats, initiatives, and procedural changes applicants should note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (NAMs guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential (New Approach Methodologies, NAMs). The key evaluative point is appropriateness to the specific research question rather than adopting a particular model category by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 application format and key features
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests for the Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH provided a 6-minute overview video describing the PF5 award structure and application format. Applicants should follow the PF5-specific format requirements and be aware that an application might be split into linked awards after peer review and before any Just-in-Time (JIT) requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants preparing DMS Plans for relevant submissions should adopt the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified in that format. This is a prescriptive format change applicants must follow where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations throughout NIH research; NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative support this expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reliability of biomedical research underpins public trust; NIH encourages a culture that values replication and reproducibility. Applicants should consider design, methods, and reporting that enable replication and reproducibility and may be mindful of highlighted topics or review emphases tied to this initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' score designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency review modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving this designation should understand it reflects a triage/selection approach where applications below a numerical cutoff (approximately top third discussed) may be labeled 'competitive but not discussed.' NIH implemented this to account for disruptions and to preserve consideration of applications that are competitive but did not reach discussion thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within CSR and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR); initial effects include changes intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that peer review processes, logistics, and possibly study section organization or procedures may be affected by centralization. NIH has provided updates on the consolidation and its early effects to help applicants anticipate how reviews may be managed.
